subject: Triangle
content: A triangle is a 3-sided polygon. Angle sum is 180°. Types: equilateral, isosceles, scalene, right-angled.

subject: Circle
content: A circle is the set of points at fixed distance (radius) from a centre. Circumference = 2πr; area = πr².

subject: Square
content: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles (90°).

subject: Cube
content: A cube is a solid with 6 square faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices.

subject: Sphere
content: A sphere is a perfectly round solid; surface area 4πr², volume (4/3)πr³.

subject: Angle
content: An angle is formed by two rays sharing an endpoint. Measured in degrees or radians. Right angle = 90°, straight = 180°.

subject: Seasons
content: Many regions have four seasons: spring, summer, autumn (fall), winter — driven by Earth's tilt and orbit.

subject: Star
content: A star is a luminous sphere of plasma held by gravity, producing energy by nuclear fusion. The Sun is a star.

subject: Planet
content: A planet orbits a star, is rounded by its own gravity, and has cleared its orbital neighbourhood (IAU definition).

subject: Noun
content: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea (e.g. student, Kenya, book, freedom).

subject: Verb
content: A verb expresses action or state (e.g. run, think, is, become).

subject: Adjective
content: An adjective describes a noun (e.g. bright, careful, large).

subject: Idiom
content: An idiom is a phrase whose meaning is not literal (e.g. 'break a Gordian knot' = solve a hard problem boldly).

subject: Punctuation
content: Punctuation marks structure writing: period, comma, question mark, colon, semicolon, quotation marks, apostrophe.

subject: Collocation
content: Collocation is the habitual pairing of words (e.g. make a decision, heavy rain).

subject: Phonetic symbols
content: IPA symbols represent speech sounds. Example: /ʃ/ as in ship, /θ/ as in think.

subject: Consonant
content: Consonants are speech sounds with some airflow restriction (e.g. b, t, s, m). English has about 24 consonant sounds.

subject: Vowel
content: Vowels are open speech sounds (e.g. a, e, i, o, u sounds). English has more vowel sounds than vowel letters.

subject: Diphthong
content: A diphthong is a gliding vowel sound within one syllable (e.g. /aɪ/ in time, /ɔɪ/ in boy).

subject: Metric system
content: Metric units: metre (length), kilogram (mass), second (time), litre (volume). Prefixes: milli, centi, kilo.

subject: Non-metric measures
content: Imperial/US customary: inch, foot, yard, mile; ounce, pound; pint, gallon. Convert carefully for science work.

subject: Ginger
content: Ginger root is used in food and traditional remedies; often associated with digestion support. Not a substitute for medical advice.

subject: Garlic
content: Garlic is used in cooking; traditionally linked to heart and immune folklore. Seek professional medical advice for health use.

subject: Aloe vera
content: Aloe vera gel is commonly used on skin; internal use needs caution. Not a substitute for medical care.

subject: Chamomile
content: Chamomile tea is often used for relaxation routines. Allergies possible (daisy family).

subject: Mint
content: Mint is used for flavour; traditionally associated with digestion comfort.

subject: Male names examples
content: Example male given names: James, David, John, Michael, Daniel, Joseph, Samuel, Peter, Kevin, Brian.

subject: Female names examples
content: Example female given names: Mary, Sarah, Emily, Anna, Grace, Rachel, Elizabeth, Sophia, Hannah, Joy.
